newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says no changes to pensions until 98.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says no changes to pensions until 98.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that changes to Italy's pensions system would not be implemented until January 1, 1998, as outlined under a landmark 1995 pensions deal.

Welfare spending is shaping up to be the next big battleground in Italian politics and Prodi told a current affairs show on state television RAI that he favoured a "redistribution" rather than a reduction of spending.
Welfare spending had grown faster than gross domestic product in past years and it was time to "reverse the trend."
"We have to bear in mind the low number of years worked for some kinds of pension," he added.

Economists say the bloated system must be tackled but the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support gives Prodi a majority in parliament, is vehemently opposed to any cuts in social spending.

Refoundation almost caused the government to fall last month because of its intransigent opposition to the deployment of an Italian-led security force for Albania. Party leader Fausto Bertinotti has warned that Prodi's real test will come over welfare, which he calls the mother of all issues.
Prodi said early retirement should not be encouraged.
"We shouldn't be rewarding those who leave early," he said.
Grilled on the subject by Guilio Tremonti, a former finance minister in Silvio Berlusconi's brief centre-left government, Prodi joked: "I have no intention of retiring."
